hooks.command:
cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$cmd" ] && exit 0; echo "$cmd" | grep -qE 'jamf-cli [^|&;]* (create|update|apply|patch) ' || exit 0; echo "$cmd" | grep -q -- '--scaffold' && exit 0; msg=$(printf '[jamf-cli] Spec check for jamf-cli writes. This hook does not block the command; it applies to the body you send next.
Run the command with --scaffold first for the exact template, then check the API spec below for required fields and enums.
  Platform — fetch from specs/platform/ (filenames are abbreviated, NOT <resource>-api.json):
    blueprints              -> blueprints_api.json
    compliance-benchmarks   -> compliance_benchmark_engine.json
    platform-devices        -> device_inventory_api.json (+ device_management_action_api.json)
    platform-device-groups  -> device_group_inventory_api.json
    ddm-reports             -> declaration_reporting_service.json
    base: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jamf-Concepts/jamf-cli/main/specs/platform/
  Classic API (/JSSResource/ paths):
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jamf-Concepts/jamf-cli/main/specs/classic/resources.yaml
  Pro modern API (all other resources):
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jamf-Concepts/jamf-cli/main/specs/JamfProAPI.yaml is 1.6 MB and WebFetch truncates it
    before paths:, so do not WebFetch it. Find the path key with Bash:
      curl -fsSL <that URL> | grep "^  /.*<distinctive word of the resource>"
    then print that one key with awk, as step 2 of the jamf-cli skill shows.
    app-installers* -> WebFetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jamf-Concepts/jamf-cli/main/specs/AppInstallers.yaml'); jq -n --arg m "$msg" '{hookSpecificOutput:{hookEventName:"PreToolUse",additionalContext:$m}}'; exit 0
